summary:
Photon is an offline-first astronaut health monitoring platform for long-duration space missions. It brings together crew vital signs, sleep, mental wellness, radiation exposure, cabin environment data, daily countermeasures, and mission hazards in one responsive dashboard. Photon uses configurable health ranges and an explainable rule engine to identify unusual readings, trends, missing information, and possible risks, then presents alerts and recommended next steps.

The project addresses the challenge of supporting astronaut health when real-time communication with Earth may be delayed or unavailable. By allowing crews to record and assess data locally, Photon helps them make informed decisions before ground support responds. It is important because deep-space missions require more autonomous, privacy-aware, and reliable health-support tools.
details:
Photon is an offline-capable astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed for long-duration space missions. It combines vital-sign tracking, mental-wellness check-ins, environmental monitoring, radiation exposure, daily routines, crew status, alerts, and explainable health assessments in one mission-control dashboard.

The system analyzes simulated crew measurements such as heart rate, SpO₂, temperature, sleep, blood pressure, activity, cabin conditions, and radiation dose. It compares readings against configurable reference ranges, detects concerning trends, identifies missing data, and generates clear alerts and recommended actions. Medical officers can view crew-level status while astronauts have role-based access to their own information.

Photon’s intended impact is to help crews recognize risks early when communication with Earth is delayed, limited, or unavailable. It is designed as decision support—not a diagnostic tool—and emphasizes transparency, privacy, offline use, and explainable findings.

We used React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, IndexedDB, and PWA technology for the responsive frontend. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, JWT authentication, and ReportLab for reports. The project uses simulated mission data rather than hardware sensors, but its architecture can later connect to certified wearable, habitat, and radiation-monitoring devices.

Photon is creative because it combines medical, environmental, behavioral, and operational data into one dark mission-control experience built specifically for spaceflight conditions. Our team considered offline reliability, crew privacy, usability on desktop and mobile, role-based access, alert clarity, data completeness, and the need to avoid presenting automated screening as a medical diagnosis.
